Bristlecone v1.4.1 — preliminary weather learning and accuracy fixes

Mountain weather now bundles a real trained temperature correction. Small quantile regression trees learn the difference between the physical weather estimate and 187 time-matched observations from 31 public US stations. The model runs on the device; it does not send your position or trip to an AI service.

This is a deliberately bounded pilot. It applies only to NWS inputs inside the training ranges, with terrain available and no overlapping nearby-station adjustment. The data covers one October day and grid-to-target elevation differences of about −57 to +187 metres. Canada, other seasons, larger elevation differences and unsupported conditions keep the physical model. This release does not claim broadly validated mountain-forecast accuracy. The later-hour improvement was very small, and the displayed uncertainty range is not a calibrated safety guarantee. Official forecasts, alerts and observed conditions remain essential.

The fixed model was tested on unseen stations, later hours with a one-hour training gap, and later hours at unseen stations. Validation evaluates the actual exported JavaScript trees and fallback gates. No test targets or test-range extrema are used to fit a fold. Data provenance and reproducible evaluation are included under `tools/weather/`.

Several weather bugs are also fixed:

- Missing official snow-level data no longer acts like a zero-metre reading and halves the estimate.
- A trail report without a temperature no longer acts like a 0 °C measurement.
- Learned temperature residuals are counted once in the likely range, and crossing quantiles cannot invert it.
- Freezing and snow-level calculations use the same bounded learned correction and report adjustment as the temperature model. They verify a genuine crossing, so a learned-model boundary cannot masquerade as a freezing level.
- A temperature report that already agrees with the corrected model no longer adds the learned bias a second time.
- Forecast uncertainty follows the forecast's issue age, even when its cached response was fetched recently.

The established on-device gait learning, GPS-gap estimates, trail-report filtering, map downloads and privacy controls remain available.

Downloads:

- Android 8.0+: `Bristlecone-1.4.1-android.apk` (test build).
- iPhone/iPad, iOS 16+: `Bristlecone-1.4.1-ios-unsigned.ipa` (AltStore/SideStore sideload format).

Sources: NWS forecasts and observations; USGS 3DEP, SRTM and GMTED2010 terrain via AWS Terrain Tiles. The derived correction is Krummholz processing, not an official NWS product or endorsement.
